column1: # 30장 말투 지시(11-10). 열: 조각 앞머리 → 지시(영어, 짧게). @scene 행은 장면 설명. "Gracias."(엄마, 배낭여행자)는 앞머리가 겹쳐 지시하지 않고 장면 설명에 넣는다.

column2: August again, a year later, the Gràcia street festival. Yuna, who now lives in Barcelona and works in the workshop, has won the neighbours' vote for a street decorated with clocks, including a three-metre cardboard grandfather clock that Marc made move with an old washing-machine motor. Marc calls it the ugliest thing he has ever made; Yuna calls it "precioso" (lovely). Warm, settled, gently humorous.
warm, content, a year later

column1: Es lo más feo que he hecho
column2: deadpan, looking at his cardboard pendulum
fond, sincere, disagreeing with him; stress "precioso"
dry, a hint of pride
lightly amused, fond

column2: Saturday, the day before the festival. Yuna and Marc pick up Yuna's mother at the airport; she has come from Busan with three Spanish words written on a paper. Marc greets her in Korean, "Annyeonghaseyo", which he practised for a week, with bad pronunciation; she laughs and says in Korean his pronunciation is awful but his face is fine. Yuna translates it kindly, not quite exactly. Light, warm.
warm, a little nervous
a Korean greeting he practised for a week, careful and clumsy, with a Catalan accent
a little anxious, wanting to know
a small smile, softening the translation

Montse's patio. Yuna's mother lived here as a three-year-old in 1978 and says she remembers nothing, yet she stops still at the gate. Montse comes out and sees her for the first time in forty-nine years: "La niña", then in Catalan "la meva nena". The mother says one careful Spanish word, "Gracias", tongue between her teeth for the Castilian "c", and gives back the postcard. Montse answers that the thanks are hers. Deeply moved but quiet; Montse does not cry in front of people.
quiet, holding breath
almost a whisper, overwhelmed; first Spanish, then Catalan as if to a small child
tender, holding her face; "filla" is Catalan for daughter
softly, smiling through feeling
tender, quiet

That night, everyone goes down to the workshop basement: Montse, Vale, old Joan from Sitges, Yuna's mother and Yuna. At nine o'clock the clock plays the grandmother's song; Yuna's mother recognises it at once and, for the first time in her life, hums it, with Montse and Yuna joining in. Vale whispers a joke to Yuna. Hushed, moving, then a small laugh.
hushed

column1: A las nueve en punto, el reloj cantó.
column2: very quiet, full of wonder
whispered, teary and teasing, Rioplatense

Sunday, the festival. A young Korean backpacker, lost and red from the heat, asks Yuna for directions in slow, careful beginner Spanish, the way Yuna spoke a year ago. Yuna answers in Spanish, kindly and simply, so the girl can practise. The girl says "Gracias" with a perfect Castilian "th". When she asks if Yuna is from here, Yuna answers yes and welcomes her. The last scene of the book: calm, warm, full circle.
bright, happy, festival day
slow and careful, a beginner, a little lost and shy
slow and clear for a learner, kind; a small joke about getting lost
warm, simple
careful, curious, polite
calm and sure, a quiet smile; stress "Bienvenida"
